title: Reference Cycles

answers: A Weak link is cheaper to clone than an Rc
Two Rc links in a cycle never reach zero, so nothing is freed
The compiler refuses to build a cyclic Rc graph
writing.exampleCaption: The child points back with Weak, so the cycle never forms.
writing.explanation: Two Rc handles pointing at each other never reach a count of zero, so neither is freed. Weak<T> is the answer: it does not count towards ownership and must be upgraded before use, which turns a parent pointer into something that can legitimately be gone.
writing.feedback: Ownership should flow one way; the back-reference observes without owning.
writing.question: Why should the parent link be Weak?
writing.rule: Weak does not keep a value alive, so upgrade() may return None.
writing.success: You can name which direction owns and which merely observes.
writing.summary: Rust prevents data races, not leaks — a cycle can still strand memory.
writing.task: Explain where a parent pointer should be Weak rather than Rc.
